name: Claude Fix Tests

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [heavy-test-failure, smoke-test-failure]
  pull_request_review:
    types: [submitted]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run_url:
        description: "URL of the failing GitHub Actions run"
        required: false
        type: string
      inspect_evals_ref:
        description: "inspect_evals branch/tag/commit to checkout (defaults to the branch this workflow is dispatched from)"
        required: false
        type: string
      smoke_failing_evals:
        description: "Comma-separated eval names to test the smoke-test fix path (e.g. gaia_level2,kernelbench)"
        required: false
        type: string

# Per-job concurrency is set on each fix-* job below. This workflow-level
# group only serves to satisfy zizmor's `concurrency-limits` rule with a
# group that never collides with any per-job group, and never cancels.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-meta-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

# Workflow-level permissions are restrictive by default. Jobs that need
# elevated scopes (e.g. AWS OIDC for Claude on Bedrock) declare them locally.
# Git push and PR creation use a GitHub App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN), so this
# workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs contents/pull-requests write.
permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read  # list prior runs for self-imposed rate limiting and CI-failure inspection

jobs:
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Job 1: Fix failures reported by CI or manual dispatch
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    name: Fix failing tests from CI
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.smoke_failing_evals == '')
      || (github.event_name == 'repository_dispatch' && github.event.action == 'heavy-test-failure')

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read         # `gh run view`/`gh run download` to inspect failing CI runs
      id-token: write       # AWS OIDC for Claude on Bedrock via aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials
    concurrency:
      group: claude-fix-ci-${{ github.run_id }}

    steps:
      # Use a GitHub App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so that PRs opened by this
      # job trigger CI — PRs created with GITHUB_TOKEN don't fire downstream
      # `on: pull_request` workflows. Permissions come from the App's
      # installation settings, not from this workflow's `permissions:` block.
      - name: Generate App token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Scope the token to what these jobs exercise (push commits/branches,
          # open and update PRs, comment on issues/PRs). Without an explicit
          # permission-* input the token inherits the App installation's full
          # permission set.
          permission-contents: write

          ref: ${{ inputs.inspect_evals_ref || '' }}
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
